title.en: Index numbers: simple and weighted price indices

hook.en: A family that spent ₹20,000 a month in 2020 needs much more now for the same basket of food, fuel and fares. An *index* number puts that change in one figure.

objectives.en: Compute simple and weighted aggregative price indices
Use Laspeyres, Paasche and Fisher formulas
Know the uses and limits of index numbers

title.en: Compute simple and weighted aggregative price indices
Use Laspeyres, Paasche and Fisher formulas
Know the uses and limits of index numbers

say.en: A family that spent 20,000 rupees a month in 2020 needs much more now for the same basket of food, fuel and fares. An index number puts that change in one figure. In this lesson: Compute simple and weighted aggregative price indices.
Use Laspeyres, Paasche and Fisher formulas.
Know the uses and limits of index numbers.

body.en: An *index* number measures the change in a group of related variables between a base year (index 100) and a current year. Simple aggregative: $P_{01} = \dfrac{\sum p_1}{\sum p_0}\times 100$. Weighted by quantities: Laspeyres (base quantities) $L = \dfrac{\sum p_1q_0}{\sum p_0q_0}\times 100$; Paasche (current quantities) $P = \dfrac{\sum p_1q_1}{\sum p_0q_1}\times 100$; Fisher $F = \sqrt{L\,P}$. A cost of living index uses the basket of a group of consumers.

points.en: L uses q₀; P uses q₁

Weighted by quantities: Laspeyres (base quantities) $L = \dfrac{\sum p_1q_0}{\sum p_0q_0}\times 100$; Paasche (current quantities) $P = \dfrac{\sum p_1q_1}{\sum p_0q_1}\times 100$; Fisher $F = \sqrt{L\,P}$. say.en: An index number measures the change in a group of related variables between a base year index 100 and a current year. Simple aggregative: P 01 equals the sum of p 1 over the sum of p 0 times 100. Weighted by quantities: Laspeyres base quantities L equals the sum of p 1q 0 over the sum of p 0q 0 times 100; Paasche current quantities P equals the sum of p 1q 1 over the sum of p 0q 1 times 100; Fisher F equals the square root of L P. A cost of living index uses the basket of a group of consumers. Base year equals 100.
L uses q 0; P uses q 1.
Fisher equals the square root of L times P, the "ideal" index.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Prices of three items in 2020 were 20, rupees 50, rupees 30 rupees and in 2025 25, rupees 60, rupees 45 rupees. Find the simple aggregative price index for 2025 2020 equals 100.
Σp 0 equals 100, Σp 1 equals 130.
P 01 equals 130 over 100 times 100 equals 130.
So the answer is 130: prices rose 30 percent.

heading.en: L for last time, P for present

body.en: Laspeyres weights by the base (old) basket, Paasche by the present basket. When people switch away from items that got dearer, L usually comes out above P; Fisher sits between.
